findings.title: String#<< mutates the literal and website_host may be nil-safe issue in ends_with check
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses `<<`, which mutates the string literal in place (fine per call since literals are fresh in Ruby without frozen_string_literal, but it is still a mutating operator on a temporary, and inconsistent with the rest of the method). More important: when the website host is a parent domain with an unrelated suffix match, e.g. website 'ample.com' and discourse 'example.com', the check is a plain suffix match on '.ample.com' so it is correct only because of the leading dot; the logic is fragile but works. The real issue is the first branch: when website_host equals discourse_host the path is appended, so 'http://example.com' with no path yields 'example.com' plus '' which is fine, but a website with a trailing slash yields 'example.com/' shown to users. Consider normalizing empty or root paths.

findings.title: Hostname comparison uses discourse_host.split on possibly nil or differing host lengths
findings.body: The method calls `discourse_host.split('.')` and compares segment counts without guarding against discourse_host being nil or having a port. For the 'same length' branch the comparison `split('.')[1..-1]` on a two-label host like 'example.com' is skipped only because length > 2 is required, but a website host with a different label count falls into the else branch where `website_host` is used directly, which can leak the full website host for unrelated sites. Behavior is not fully specified and is untested for subdomain cases such as www vs bare domain.

findings.title: Rescue modifier swallows all errors from URI parsing and the path is recomputed multiple times
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` is computed once for the host, then `URI(website.to_s)` is re-parsed on every branch. Parsing is repeated needlessly and, if the website is malformed, `URI(...).path` in the matched branches could raise after the host check succeeded. Parse once and reuse.

findings.title: Template now depends on model.website_name, which is never shown to be set for the Ember model
findings.body: The template switches from the removed computed `websiteName` to `model.website_name`. That is a server-serialized attribute and is only present when `include_website_name?` is true, so the link text is absent for users whose website is blank, which is intended, but the `title` and href still use `model.website` which may be restricted by untrusted_attributes for anonymous users while website_name is not restricted, so anonymous viewers can see the website path (including path) even when the website field itself is hidden for TL0 users.

findings.title: website_name is not subject to the untrusted_attributes restriction
findings.body: website and bio fields are hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers via untrusted_attributes, but website_name (which exposes the website host and now the full path) is serialized with only `website.present?` as its guard. The spec for TL0 anonymous users does not include website_name, so the leak is untested and the privacy control is bypassed.

findings.title: Spec does not cover the case where website has no path or a trailing slash
findings.body: The new tests only cover 'http://example.com/user'. There is no test for a bare domain website (e.g. 'http://example.com') on the same-host branch, which would show whether the output is 'example.com' or 'example.com/' and whether the rescue path yields nil. No test covers a malformed website or the TL0 anonymous visibility of website_name.
